meta.title: URL Shortener: asymmetric write and read paths

components.label: Client: create
components.explanation: Submits a long URL, with an optional custom alias and expiry, and receives a short code. Roughly 40 writes/sec at 100M new links/month.

components.label: Write service
components.explanation: Owns correctness and uniqueness of codes. Scales independently of the redirect path.

components.label: ID generator
components.explanation: A coordinator leases (start, end) ranges of 1,000-10,000 ids to each app server, which increments locally. One round trip per range instead of per URL; a crashed server only wastes its unused tail.

components.label: Key-value store
components.explanation: urls(code PK, long_url, created_at, expires_at, owner_id, custom_alias). Every access is a single-key point lookup with no joins: DynamoDB, Cassandra or sharded MySQL keyed by code.

components.label: Client: click code
components.explanation: The path users feel. Must stay under ~50ms; 4,000+ redirects/sec at a 100:1 read:write ratio.

components.label: Redirect service
components.explanation: Checks Redis first, falls back to the key-value store on a miss and backfills the cache. 301 is cheaper at scale; 302 is needed when every click must be counted server-side.

components.label: Redis cache
components.explanation: Click distributions are power-law, so a small set of hot links absorbs most traffic. Long URLs never change, so TTLs can be hours to days.

components.label: Kafka / Kinesis
components.explanation: Carries code, timestamp, referrer and IP-derived geo. Keeps analytics writes off the redirect's critical path.

cards.title: Write path
items: ~40 writes/sec: optimise for unique, hard-to-guess codes
Range-allocated counters avoid a per-request round trip

cards.title: Read path
items: 100:1 to 1000:1 read:write; spend the scaling budget here
Redis first, key-value store on a miss, then backfill

cards.title: Analytics
items: Never write analytics synchronously on a redirect
301 under-counts repeat visits; 302 counts every click
